actor.finalResponse: I recommend a three-turn sequence: show paragraph A and ask question A, then show B and ask question B, then show C and ask question C. Put each question in its own turn. Questions grouped in one turn share the state from before that group, so grouping them would not give question C the answers to A and B. A sequence is a distinct authored journey form, although a linear graph can also express a fixed A-to-B-to-C path. I would specify the history requirement explicitly: each later turn should receive the earlier turns that respondent actually reached, including their answers. Before running it, inspect the compiled respondent packets to confirm that exposure and answer history match that requirement. I would need the exact paragraph text and the question after each before building the request.
uncertainties: The supplied contract does not establish that a linear graph has the same history semantics as a sequence.
The exact earlier-answer content included in each later packet needs confirmation through inspection.
